item.content:encoded:
IMO I see this hub as us taking something absolutely disgusting and turning it into a group of people getting together to have a little fun, which seems to be a little scarce on mainsite these days.

Exactly.

Ihp, I know you mean well, but here's something we should all consider; when something remotely bothersome happens (say disguting anon hate), should we let it bother and anger us for the rest of our days, letting every hint of that occurrence ruffle our jimmies and overall make our experience on this wiki worse, or should we instead unite as one to turn something bad into an inside joke — something for us to laugh about, rather than to grimace at and ignore.

This is the beuty of the Internet. We, as a people, can come together and do something — anything — incredible. That is dickbottle. Dickbottle is the SCP Wiki coming togther and shedding light on an otherwise distasteful situation. And instead of treating it as a burden we took it in as a joke, and we had a good time. And, hey, I don't know about you, but I joined the wiki to have a good time.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Frankly, speaking as one of the early writers for this canon (Coffee Date), i didn’t intend it just to spite the hateful individual; I wrote it because the site as a whole has a type of atmosphere about it that highly lacks the humanizing content that I really enjoy as a reader. I thought the bottledick joke was funny. Any further contributions will be not directly about that, but about the impact it (and in-universe jokes like it) impact the social culture of the site they occur in. Cause I think it’s neat. We went from Mary Sue lolfoundation and swapped sides to emotionless morally fucked robot characters, and I don’t personally enjoy either of those things. I’m writing for the fun of it.

Do I enjoy writing knowing that it’s exactly what the anon hated? Yes absolutely. Was it why I wrote it? Not really. I wanted to give Kondraki in this series a little more depth. In fact, I was SPECIFICALLY looking to make it a little More than just “haha bottledick”. The discord a lot of the ideas generated from has more in store for this series than just penis in bottle jokes.

You of course have your right to an opinion. But I will say this; what started out as spite has changed completely. Now it’s a testament to people writing whatever they want just for shits and giggles. Because we enjoy it. Because it’s fun. And that’s what the original bottledick tale was really about. It was a funny joke one-off than became infectious because of one persons anger. We turned that hate into something that makes all of us happy.

Shrugs. Maybe I’m looking too deeply into something I helped make.

item.content:encoded:
If you up Vote or down vote for this stuff because you like or don't like the content then you are on solid ground. But if you are doing either to try and send a message, either to the guy who started all this, or the writers who decided to make this, then I feel like you guys are on shaky ground here. It gets shakier if you start encouraging people to up or down vote based on your opinions of the writers, or of the anons who do or don't like it.

In my opinion? I think that adding the off-site context was unnecessary. The context was already provided in the environment where it was necessary: that of the other website where all of this stuff to place, and the idea for this whole thing was originally brewed. However, the fact that people who have no idea of the original context still thought that there was something interesting, funny, or otherwise worth exploring in the core concept of "bottle dick" seems to indicate that there is actually something to this idea other than mere spite.

I would encourage that the canon curator replaced the references to all the off-site drama by simply saying that if you understand the context then you know why this was done. I think that's all that really needed to be said about that particular person.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I am not sure if this is a really a canon. Surely it is more of a series.

"That one time Kondraki got a bottle stuck on his penis and everyone made fun of him" doesn't strike me as an essential setting premise in the vein of "the Foundation never existed", "the UN killed God and the world broke", or "stories set at a site built next to a multiversal nexus". Nor does "Foundation employees are humans who do dumb stuff and get embarrassed" seem as thematically cogent as "low urban fantasy and slice-of-life horror set against the backdrop of the American South" or "transhumanist new weird adventure fiction in a world where weird science went industrial".

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The only thing I really feel when looking at this hub is disappointment in all the contributors— actually, that's an understatement. Clef himself said that Third Date was "fueled by a martini, spite, and rage at anyone who wants to use Clef to justify their fuckboyish behavior". — it was posted with immature intent, and has lead to immature content. It's a joke that a seventh grader would roll his eyes at. But that's not what I'm posting about. I'm posting about the fact that this entire canon is legitimizing off-site drama in a toxic manner.

Posted without context, I could easily downvote all of these and move on for being immature humor. With the context, we have a problem. You are spreading the message of the troll, and therefore feeding it. Now that it is posted to the wiki — the very site he was attacking — you have legitimized him by directly acknowledged that he exists.

Flawed metaphor incoming: imagine if the New York Times decided to run a hit piece on the guy in the comments section of their website who keeps posting ASCII art of swastikas. They wouldn't, because they're acknowledging them, and therefore spreading their message. That's what's being done here— by posting the context to this aberration, you are giving him an official platform on the wiki. Hell, I want to argue that Third Date alone gave him a platform. I trust the contributors on the site to not emulate the troll's behavior, but the same can't be said of those who solely read the content, or experience it through Tumblr, Youtube, Facebook, Reddit, etc. By writing an insult to one troll, you may have just spawned twenty more.

That's why I'm downvoting all of these, and will downvote every single one that's posted. They all have the potential for a single toxic individual to infect the views of others, and that is downright inexcusable on this site. My disappointment in the contributors is immeasurable.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The level of detail given about the harassment that went on is probably detracting from the fiction a little, IMO. Having also personally experienced the ranting and anon-messaging of people who police content, they and their opinions don't really deserve this much attention1, even when kept anonymous. If I stumbled upon this as a new site member and ended up reading unexpected details with Tumblr post links about someone getting told to kill themself on the hub page of a canon, it'd probably feel more than a little uncomfortable.

I support the notion of writing to spite someone if it's over something egregiously stupid that shouldn't even be controversial in the first place, which this is, but I wish the specific details of the negative backstory were in the author post instead.

That said, this gained upvotes fast, so I'm probably in the minority for feeling like this. Overall, it's still worth a +1. Edit: Honestly, after reading this again and reading more comments about the things I'm talking about, I'm removing my vote. The inclusion of Tumblr drama hyperlinks on a mainsite page is cringeworthy in and of itself, and there's only so much you can do with this basic idea anyway. And I'll second that it doesn't really make sense as a canon. There's no massive overarching AU going on here like there typically is with canons. This is a hub of tales about a one-dimensional middle-school-level penis joke, and not much else about the Foundation universe has changed. I've upvoted a few of these tales for the humor they did convey, but the concept is wearing out real fast.

Footnotes
1. Edit: To quote IHP below: "You are spreading the message of the troll, and therefore feeding it. Now that it is posted to the wiki — the very site he was attacking — you have legitimized him by directly acknowledged that he exists."
